source.title: Item 12 — 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund — South Yorkshire Police and Crime Panel, 22 June 2026

facts.note: The Police Fund is now hosted inside the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority (SYMCA), which absorbed the Police & Crime Commissioner function in May 2024 when the PCC role transferred to the South Yorkshire Mayor. This paper is what a Police & Crime Panel gets: a revenue-outturn covering paper on the Police Fund. The substantive treasury reporting for the same financing entity (loan book, CFR, prudential indicators, maturity profile, MRP policy) lives in SYMCA's own treasury reports to its Audit, Standards and Risk Committee — a separate paper series held under E47000002 in the record set. This mg476 paper is not the place to look for a loan book.

facts.value: SYMCA Capital Financing (p.1, £m): Debt interest — Budget 1.7 / Actual 1.2 / Variance 0.5 (29.3%) underspend. Investment income — Budget (4.0) / Actual (6.5) / Variance 2.5 (62.9%) overachievement. MRP — Budget 4.7 / Actual 5.6 / Variance (0.9) (20.0%) overspend. Total SYMCA Capital Financing Budget 2.3 / Actual 0.3 / Variance 2.1 (87.7%). SYP Capital Financing Costs (p.3, £'000): Budget 700 / Outturn 5,800 / Variance (5,200) — this is deliberate revenue-financing of capital to avoid new PWLB, not an interest-cost overrun (paper is explicit about the mechanic).

source.title: Item 12 — 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund — Summary Table p.1, SYP Detail p.3

facts.note: Sum-check on SYMCA Capital Financing: 1.2 debt interest + (6.5) investment income + 5.6 MRP = 0.3 actual — ties to printed 0.3. Investment income (£6.5m) is 5.4x debt interest (£1.2m) at SYMCA level; consistent with the small ~£27m PWLB book (our file) and the paper's 'higher than predicted cash balances' wording. The MRP overspend of £0.9m is explicitly framed as 'SYMCA took the opportunity to pay down legacy debt' (p.2). The £5.2m SYP capital-financing overspend and the £0.5m debt-interest underspend together represent ~£5.7m of unbudgeted cash directed towards debt avoidance/paydown during 2025/26.

facts.value: Paper refers three times (p.1 Summary; p.2 twice) to the pre-transfer OPCC's 'historic under provision of debt charges' — quoted phrase 'the inherited Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) omissions' (p.1) and 'the inherited issues from the former OPCC around historic under provision of debt charges' (p.2). No numerical size of the historic gap, no year identified, no planned catch-up profile disclosed in this paper. Current strategy: divert revenue underspends to (a) additional MRP charges, (b) revenue-financing of capital in place of new borrowing, (c) targeted reserves top-ups.

source.title: Item 12 — 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund — pp.1, 2

facts.note: Unusually candid framing for a covering revenue-outturn paper. Most councils that inherit an MRP under-provision would surface the issue and the catch-up profile in a treasury management strategy or a standalone MRP policy statement, not in the Police Panel outturn narrative. The wording ('omissions', 'historic under provision') sits at the plain-English end of the sector's vocabulary for this class of issue. The SYMCA treasury paper (E47000002) is where the quantum and catch-up path would be.

facts.value: Home Office capitalisation direction for 2025/26 legacy costs confirmed May 2026 (p.4). Legacy costs falling to SYP £2,510k: Hillsborough Civil Claims £919k; Child Sexual Exploitation Civil Claims £238k; Operation Stovewood £1,353k. 'These costs will be charged to revenue accounts over the next 20 years rather than representing an immediate draw on revenue budgets.' Enabled SYMCA to release £2.4m of legacy-cost provisions back into usable reserves (p.4).

source.title: Item 12 — 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund — Legacy Costs table p.4

facts.note: This is a Home Office direction specific to inherited legacy claims for police forces — sector-wide category (Hillsborough, CSA / Op Stovewood matters), not the same class of instrument as MHCLG's Exceptional Financial Support capitalisation directions to distress councils (Thurrock, Woking, Croydon, Slough). Continuation of the 2024/25 direction. The mechanical treasury effect is that £2.51m of what would have been in-year revenue cost becomes 20-year debt-service, adding to CFR. Amount is small in the context of the £358.8m outturn but material to the reserves narrative (£2.4m provisions release drove the net +£0.4m reserves increase).

facts.value: Approved budget £362.1m included a £5.3m planned draw on usable reserves. £3.3m surplus reduced the draw; £2.4m provisions release from the capitalisation direction added back. Net effect: usable reserves +£0.4m between March 2025 and March 2026. But: 'the Fund's Medium Term Financial Plan continues to show that general reserves are expected to fall below prudent levels by the end of the five-year period.' (p.4)

source.title: Item 12 — 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund — Impact on Reserves p.4

facts.note: Arithmetic: 5.3 planned draw − 3.3 surplus − 2.4 provisions release = (0.4) → +£0.4m reserves. TIES. The five-year prudent-level warning is what elevates this from a good-news outturn to a 'structural pressure still there' story — but the MTFP itself is not in this paper. The MTFP would be a separate paper to note against if it surfaces.

facts.value: Final capital outturn £15.1m against £17.9m approved capital programme budget for 2025/26 (p.3). Split: £10.2m ICT and operational equipment (incl. joint projects with Humberside Police); £3.7m vehicle replacement programme; £1.2m building improvements (p.3-4).

summary.text:
South Yorkshire Police and Crime Panel took the 2025/26 outturn report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund on 22 June 2026. The paper is a 4-page covering revenue-outturn document by Gareth Sutton (SYMCA S151, Executive Director for Resources and Investment), with three tables — Summary Revenue Outturn (p.1), SYP Detailed Revenue Outturn (p.3) and Legacy Costs Capitalised under Home Office direction (p.4) — plus narrative on income, expenditure, capital, legacy costs and reserves. Recommendation was 'note the contents'.

The Police Fund is now hosted inside the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority (SYMCA) following the May 2024 transfer of the Police & Crime Commissioner function to the South Yorkshire Mayor. The substantive treasury reporting for the same financing entity (loan book, CFR, prudential indicators, maturity profile, MRP policy) lives in the SYMCA treasury paper series to SYMCA's Audit, Standards and Risk Committee — held separately under the E47000002 record set. This mg476 paper is not where the loan book sits.

Loan-book reconciliation is not possible against this paper. Our file at 31 March 2026 shows 18 loans / £26,984,000 / weighted 4.3416% under SOUTH YORKSHIRE MAYORAL COM AUT - POLICE, all MATURITY profile — but the paper prints no loan-book table, no PWLB total, no weighted rate and no maturity profile. Per PIPELINE guidance the loan-book claim is kept out of the email entirely. A timing quirk on our own file (1 loan on 31 Dec 2025 rising to 18 loans on 31 Mar 2026) reflects the novation of legacy OPCC PWLB stock onto the SYMCA - POLICE borrower code after the transfer, not fresh drawdowns; consistent with the paper's statement that 'the need for external borrowing was deferred'.

Balance-sheet identity is not computable — the paper carries none of CFR, external borrowing stock, or other long-term liabilities. What DOES tie: every revenue arithmetic check on the paper's own numbers reconciles (Summary table, SYMCA Capital Financing, SYP detailed variances, Legacy Costs total, Reserves movement). That is what proves the read.

Two things in the paper stand out for a treasurer. The first is unusually candid disclosure (three times, p.1 and p.2) of 'the inherited Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) omissions' and 'the inherited issues from the former OPCC around historic under provision of debt charges' — the wording sits at the plain-English end of the sector's vocabulary for this class of issue, and the size of the historic gap is not disclosed here (would be in a treasury paper or MRP policy statement). The second is the active pay-down strategy the paper describes: £0.9m MRP overspend explicitly to pay down legacy debt, £5.2m unbudgeted revenue-financing of capital in place of new borrowing, £0.5m debt-interest underspend from deferred external borrowing — ~£6.6m of 2025/26 favourable variance systematically directed at debt avoidance/paydown across SYMCA and SYP.

The Home Office capitalisation direction for 2025/26 legacy costs (Hillsborough £919k, CSE £238k, Op Stovewood £1,353k = £2.51m in total) was confirmed in May 2026 (p.4). These costs will be charged to revenue over 20 years rather than in-year. A knock-on effect is the release of £2.4m of legacy provisions back into usable reserves, which drove the net +£0.4m reserves position for the year despite a £5.3m planned draw. The MTFP still shows general reserves 'expected to fall below prudent levels by the end of the five-year period' (p.4).

No officer email address is printed anywhere in the paper. The author is named on the front sheet as Gareth Sutton, Executive Director for Resources and Investment (SYMCA S151), without address. Any officer contact would need to be sourced from SYMCA's own site or the ModernGov committee-membership pages — not from this paper. Meeting has passed (22 June 2026), no forward Police Panel treasury item date printed. A short qualitative email is drafted below on the strength of the debt-avoidance narrative and the capitalisation-direction context, but the paper is genuinely thin on quantitative treasury content and the draft is correspondingly light. Goes into 'drafted — needs an address' state pending an officer lookup.

officer.subject: Your inherited MRP omissions, and the ~£6.6m of underspend you redirected at debt this year
officer.body:
Dear [NAME],

Apologies for the cold email — PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're a small platform that carries PWLB rates at both fixings each working day, monthly local-authority-to-local-authority lending, every council's PWLB loan book, and a lightweight academy for treasury officers. The data side is free and stays free. The one-page brochure is at pwlbtoday.com/brochure if it helps to circulate internally.

To keep the data and training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how each authority's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Below are a few thoughts on your 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund as taken to the Police and Crime Panel on 22 June. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your paper is unusually plain-spoken on the underlying position and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

What stood out first was how directly the paper names the inherited MRP position. Three separate references — 'the inherited Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) omissions' on page 1, and 'the inherited issues from the former OPCC around historic under provision of debt charges' twice on page 2 — is more candour on a legacy MRP under-provision than we see in most covering papers. It's the sort of framing that reads as if the strategy is actively addressing the problem rather than working around it, and it made the rest of the outturn narrative land differently.

The second thing that stood out was how much of the 2025/26 favourable variance you systematically redirected at debt. £0.9m MRP overspend, described in your own words as SYMCA taking the opportunity to pay down legacy debt (p.2). £5.2m unbudgeted revenue contribution to the capital programme at SYP to avoid new external borrowing (p.2 and p.3 narratives). £0.5m debt-interest underspend from deferred external borrowing (p.2). Together that is around £6.6m of in-year underspend directed at debt avoidance or paydown across the Fund. It is a consistent, mechanical response to the inherited position — not a policy change, more a systematic deployment of every pound of favourable variance the year gave you.

One quiet knock-on we noticed on page 4 was that the Home Office capitalisation direction confirmed in May 2026 (£2.51m for Hillsborough, CSE and Operation Stovewood) enabled the £2.4m provisions release that in turn drove the net +£0.4m reserves position for the year. Without the direction, the reserves picture would have been materially different. Your MTFP still shows general reserves falling below prudent levels by the end of the five-year period, so the underlying pressure remains — but the direction has bought a year of headroom to work with.

We hold the SYMCA - Police PWLB book on file (it's what our /pwlb-activity page tracks day-to-day, alongside the daily fixings at both certainty and standard). Your outturn paper doesn't publish the loan book, which is normal for a Police Panel covering paper, so there's nothing here to tie against — this is a note to say the data is there when the next SYMCA treasury outturn or strategy paper surfaces, and we're happy to compare notes then.

On the standing-inclusion side, CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates are putting the liability benchmark in front of everyone, and it is worth looking at even for authorities running relatively small PWLB books because it interacts directly with an active pay-down strategy of the kind your paper describes. The dynamic version is at pwlbtoday.com/liability-benchmark.

The academy is a paid product. Two sessions that would sit alongside what you're doing: an MRP session covering annuity vs equal-instalment methods and how catch-up profiles for inherited under-provisions are typically presented; and a Prudential and Treasury Code refresher on the 2021 Codes and the direction of the 2026 update. Free-account sign-up is at pwlbtoday.com/sign-up; the new-account discount runs to end of September.

If any of this lands, word of mouth is how we get in front of colleagues at other combined-authority finance teams and other police-fund treasurers — a mention to peers, or to any national police-treasury network you sit on, would do more than any campaign we could run.

Best,
[NAME]
PWLBtoday
[LinkedIn]

Source: 2025/26 Outturn Report for the South Yorkshire Police Fund, South Yorkshire Police and Crime Panel, 22 June 2026, at https://SYJAGU.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s9234/item-12-202526-outturn-report-for-the-south-yorkshire-police.pdf.
officer.hook: Unusually candid disclosure of inherited MRP omissions from the former OPCC (three references, p.1 and p.2); ~£6.6m of 2025/26 favourable variance systematically redirected at debt avoidance/paydown (MRP overspend £0.9m + revenue-financed capital £5.2m + debt-interest underspend £0.5m); Home Office capitalisation direction for 2025/26 legacy costs confirmed May 2026 (£2.51m for Hillsborough/CSE/Op Stovewood, 20-year charge) enabled the £2.4m provisions release that drove the net +£0.4m reserves position
officer.notes_for_reviewer: 1) NO OFFICER ADDRESS in the paper. Author named on front sheet as Gareth Sutton (SYMCA S151) without address. Would need SYMCA's own site or a companion SYMCA paper (E47000002 record set) to source the address. 2) NO LOAN-BOOK RECONCILIATION possible — the paper prints no book. Our file holds 18 loans / £26.98m / 4.3416% under SOUTH YORKSHIRE MAYORAL COM AUT - POLICE at 31 March 2026, but per PIPELINE the loan-book claim is kept out of the email entirely. The draft acknowledges we hold the book without quoting the number. 3) BALANCE-SHEET IDENTITY not computable — the paper prints no CFR, no external borrowing stock, no OLTL. Recorded in facts. What ties instead: every revenue arithmetic check on the paper's own numbers reconciles (Summary table, SYMCA Capital Financing, SYP detailed variances, Legacy Costs total, Reserves movement). That proves the read. 4) HOOK is qualitative not quantitative — the paper is thin on treasury numbers, so the draft leads with the inherited MRP disclosure and the systematic pay-down mechanic, both of which are quoted verbatim from the paper. 5) CAPITALISATION DIRECTION is fact-recorded as a knock-on to the reserves position, not framed as distress. This is a Home Office direction category for police forces (Hillsborough, CSA/Op Stovewood) — sector-wide, not the same instrument as MHCLG's EFS capitalisation directions to distress councils. 6) MTFP RESERVES WARNING included as one sentence — the paper's own words, not commentary. 7) MEETING HAS PASSED (22 June 2026). No forward date printed. Send timing keyed to whichever surfaces next in the mg calendar (Q1 update to the Panel, or a SYMCA treasury paper). 8) DRAFT is longer than a truly minimal courtesy note but shorter than a full reconciliation-led draft (~750 words) — the qualitative hook needs a paragraph of setup for each angle. 9) NO NATIONAL RANKING implied. 10) NO ADVICE OR RECOMMENDATION — the pay-down mechanic is described in the paper's own words, not commented on directionally. 11) NO BREAK-COST FIGURE quoted (the paper doesn't publish the book so any figure would sit in isolation and could read as advisory). 12) 'Of the councils we have read' phrasing not needed here — the observations are about their own paper. 13) COURSES named are the two most likely to fit — MRP catch-up and Prudential Code refresher; review before send whether the MRP session in the academy specifically covers inherited under-provisions or whether it's a general MRP overview. 14) LINK TO E47000002 record set not made in the email itself but flagged in the notes for continuity — a future SYMCA treasury outturn would be where a substantive reconciliation-led follow-up email could go. 15) 'JAGU' (Joint Audit and Governance Unit) is the ModernGov site name for the South Yorkshire Police and Crime Panel — using 'Police and Crime Panel' in the email since that is the panel's actual name and matches the front sheet.
